blocks.text: IMPORTANT NFORMATION ABOUT YOUR DRINKING WATER
The Town of Keysville Water System
Has Levels of Total Trihalomethanes (TTHM) Above Drinking Water Standards

Tests indicate that the Town of Keysville water system exceeded drinking water standards. Although this is not an emergency, as our customers, you have the right to know what happened, what you should do, and what we are doing to correct this situation.

To ensure satisfactory water quality, we are required to monitor for byproducts, including Total Trihalomethanes (TTI-M), on a quarterly basis. Based on test results of routine quarterly samples collected during the first quarter (January — March) 2024 through the fourth quarter (October — December) 2024, our system exceeded the standard or Primary Maximum Contaminant Level (PMCL) for TTHM. The PMCL for 'ITHM is a locational running annual average (LRAA) of 0.080 mg/L. The average concentration for based on the four calendar quarters is 0.087 mg/L.

There is not immediate health risk. If there had been, you would have been notified immediately. However, some people who drink water containing TTHM / HAA5 in excess of the MCL over many years may have an increased risk of getting cancer.
You do not need to use an alternative water supply. However, if you have specific health concerns, consult your health care provider or the Piedmont Health District office at 434-392-3984.

TTHM., along with offer disinfection byproduct, are formed when trace amounts of naturally occurring organic compounds in the raw water source combine with chlorine that is used to disinfect the treated water. The concentrations of in your drinking water can vary because of changes in source water quality, water temperature, distribution storage time, and other factors. We will continue to monitor your drinking water for TTHM. The next sample will be collected during the second week of January 2025.
For more information, please contact the Town Office at (434) 736-9551.

Please share this information with all the other people who drink this water, especially those who may not have received this notice directly (for example, people in apartments, nursing homes, schools, and businesses). You can do this by posting this notice in a public place or distributing copies by or mail.
